how: A local server answered three origins, www.example.com and api.example.com (one site) and www.example.net (another), mapped to 127.0.0.1 with --host-resolver-rules, and localhost, over HTTPS with HTTP/2 or with HTTP/1.1 only, and over plain HTTP; it kept every request as the bytes said it, headers in order with their values, and HTTP/2 the priority of its HEADERS frame (exclusive, stream it depends on, weight as on the wire). Each scenario ran in a fresh profile: a URL opened from the command line, or a page whose script navigated, submitted a form, called fetch() or sent an XHR. The pages that ran them, and the requests that set cookies for them, are left out, as are the port numbers.
